claim: The +1 nucleosome in Saccharomyces cerevisiae covers the transcription start site of most genes.
source: In Saccharomyces cerevisiae, the +1 nucleosome covers the transcription start site (TSS) of most genes.
evidence: This is stated directly in the Introduction section of the manuscript.

claim: Blocking PIC assembly resulted in promoter-specific H2A.Z accumulation.
source: Blocking PIC assembly resulted in promoter-specific H2A.Z accumulation, indicating that the PIC is required to evict H2A.Z.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the Abstract and supported by experimental data shown in Figures 1 and 2.

claim: H2A.Z eviction was unaffected upon depletion of INO80.
source: By contrast, H2A.Z eviction was unaffected upon depletion of INO80, a remodeler previously reported to displace nucleosomal H2A.Z.
evidence: This finding is stated in the Abstract and supported by data in Figure 4.

claim: Robust PIC-dependent H2A.Z eviction was observed at active and infrequently transcribed genes.
source: Robust PIC-dependent H2A.Z eviction was observed at active and infrequently transcribed genes, indicating that constitutive H2A.Z turnover is a general phenomenon.
evidence: This is stated in the Abstract and supported by data in Figures 2 and 3.

claim: Sites with strong H2A.Z turnover precisely mark transcript starts.
source: Finally, sites with strong H2A.Z turnover precisely mark transcript starts, providing a new metric for identifying cryptic and alternative sites of initiation.
evidence: This is stated in the Abstract and demonstrated in Figure 7.

claim: The SWR1 complex catalyzes the incorporation of H2A.Z into nucleosomes.
source: The incorporation of H2A.Z into nucleosomes is catalyzed by the ATP-dependent chromatin remodeling complex SWR1 (Mizuguchi et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: The SWR1 complex comprises the catalytic core protein Swr1 and 13 other polypeptides.
source: The ~1 megadalton SWR1 complex comprises the catalytic core protein Swr1, a member of the Swi2/Snf2-related ATPase, plus 13 other polypeptides (Kobor et al., 2004; Krogan et al., 2003; Mizuguchi et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: SWR1 catalyzes a histone replacement reaction that involves the coupled removal of a nucleosomal H2A-H2B dimer with the insertion of an H2A.Z-H2B dimer.
source: It catalyzes a histone replacement reaction that involves the coupled removal of a nucleosomal H2A-H2B dimer with the insertion of an H2A.Z-H2B dimer that is delivered to the enzyme by one of several histone chaperones, including Nap1, Chz1, and FACT (Luk et al., 2007, 2010; Mizuguchi et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The two H2A-H2B dimers in a homotypic H2A nucleosome are replaced sequentially by SWR1.
source: The two H2A-H2B dimers in a homotypic H2A (AA) nucleosome are replaced sequentially, first generating the heterotypic H2A/H2A.Z (AZ) nucleosome as an intermediate (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A, step I-a) and the homotypic H2A.Z (ZZ) nucleosome as the final product (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A, step I-b) (Luk et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work and illustrated in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The (H3-H4)2 tetramer remains associated with the DNA before and after each step of the SWR1 replacement reaction.
source: The (H3-H4)2 tetramer remains associated with the DNA before and after each step of the replacement reaction as no net loss of nucleosomal species occurs during the histone replacement reaction in vitro (Luk et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Substantial amount of H2A is present at promoter-proximal nucleosomes in addition to H2A.Z.
source: While it is well established that H2A.Z is enriched at the promoter-proximal nucleosomes, it is underappreciated that substantial amount of H2A is also present at these sites (Luk et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Nucleosomes in the AA, AZ and ZZ configurations can all be detected at the +1 positions of most promoters in G1-arrested cells.
source: Experiments using sequential ChIP and tiling microarray analysis have demonstrated that in a population of G1-arrested cells, nucleosomes in the AA, AZ and ZZ configurations can all be detected at the +1 positions of most promoters (Luk et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: The SWR1 reaction that generates ZZ nucleosomes is opposed by a pathway(s) that converts ZZ nucleosomes back to the AA state in a replication-independent manner.
source: This observation suggests that the SWR1 reaction that generates ZZ nucleosomes is opposed by a pathway(s) that converts ZZ nucleosomes back to the AA state in a replication-independent manner.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that multiple nucleosome configurations coexist at promoters.

claim: Rapid, constitutive H3 turnover is observed at most +1 nucleosomes.
source: Consistent with this dynamic model, rapid, constitutive H3 turnover is observed at most +1 nucleosomes (Dion et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: H3 turnover implies complete disassembly of the ZZ nucleosome.
source: Since the (H3-H4)2 tetramer is at the center of the histone core (Luger et al., 1997), H3 turnover implies complete disassembly of the ZZ nucleosome (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A, step II).
evidence: This is an inference based on the structure of the nucleosome and supported by citation.

claim: Reassembly after ZZ nucleosome disassembly likely leads to the formation of canonical AA nucleosomes.
source: Reassembly likely leads to the formation of the canonical AA nucleosomes as H2A is ~10 times more abundant than H2A.Z and SWR1 does not assemble H2A.Z nucleosomes de novo on DNA (Luk et al., 2010; West and Bonner, 1980) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A, step III).
evidence: This is an inference based on the relative abundance of H2A and H2A.Z and the properties of SWR1, supported by citations.

claim: The INO80 complex has been reported to mediate the reverse replacement reaction in which a nucleosomal H2A.Z-H2B dimer is replaced by a free H2A-H2B dimer.
source: The ATP-dependent remodeling complex INO80 has been reported to mediate the reverse replacement reaction (in which a nucleosomal H2A.Z-H2B dimer is replaced by a free H2A-H2B dimer) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A, steps I-c and I-d) (Papamichos-Chronakis et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Analysis of H2A.Z ChIP-chip showed that H2A.Z in ino80∆ cells redistributes from promoters to gene body regions as compared to wild-type cells.
source: Analysis of H2A.Z ChIP followed by microarray (ChIP-chip) showed that H2A.Z in ino80∆ cells redistributes from promoters to gene body regions as compared to wild-type cells (Papamichos-Chronakis et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Deletion mutant of ARP5 exhibited global H2A.Z accumulation especially around the promoters as demonstrated by the ChIP-exo technique.
source: Deletion mutant of ARP5, a gene encoding a critical component of the INO80 complex, exhibited global H2A.Z accumulation especially around the promoters as demonstrated by the ChIP-exo technique (Yen et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: A more recent ChIP-chip study showed that the genome-wide H2A.Z occupancy was similar in ino80∆ and wild-type cells.
source: However, the ChIP-chip data of a more recent study disagreed, showing that the genome-wide H2A.Z occupancy was similar in ino80∆ and wild-type cells (Jeronimo et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Reciprocal increase of H2A.Z and decrease of H2A genome-wide was observed after depletion of the PIC.
source: We observed reciprocal increase of H2A.Z and decrease of H2A genome-wide after depletion of the PIC.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the Introduction and supported by data in Figures 1 and 2.

claim: Nuclear depletion of Ino80 did not cause global H2A.Z accumulation.
source: By contrast, nuclear depletion of Ino80 did not cause global H2A.Z accumulation.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the Introduction and supported by data in Figure 4.

claim: The assembly of the Pol II transcription machinery and/or its activity contribute(s) to the constitutive turnover of H2A.Z at yeast promoters.
source: These findings suggest that the assembly of the Pol II transcription machinery and/or its activity contribute(s) to the constitutive turnover of H2A.Z at yeast promoters.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental findings.

claim: TBP-FRB can be dragged out of the nucleus in a rapamycin-dependent manner by the FKBP12 tag on the pre-ribosome.
source: When fused to the FKBP12-rapamycin-binding domain (FRB), TBP-FRB can be dragged out of the nucleus in a rapamycin-dependent manner by the FKBP12 tag on the pre-ribosome (Haruki et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work describing the anchor-away technique.

claim: Previous studies showed yeast cells expressing SPT15-FRB rapidly depleted TBP from Pol II promoters, blocked Pol II recruitment and shut off transcription within 1 hr of rapamycin treatment.
source: Previous studies have shown yeast cells expressing SPT15-FRB (hereafter referred to as TBP-FRB) rapidly depleted TBP from Pol II promoters, blocked Pol II recruitment and shut off transcription within 1 hr of rapamycin treatment (Grimaldi et al., 2014; Haruki et al., 2008; Wong et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: In the experiments, TBP-FRB relocalized to the cytoplasm with similar kinetics as previously reported.
source: In our experiments, TBP-FRB relocalized to the cytoplasm with similar kinetics (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: The IP efficiency of H2A.Z ChIP was consistently over 80%.
source: Given that H2A.Z is the only H2A variant in budding yeast and the IP efficiency was consistently over 80% (Figure 1—figure supplement 3), the flow-through (FT) of the IP reaction was highly enriched for the homotypic AA nucleosomes (referred to as the H2A nucleosomes hereafter) and the IP fraction was enriched for the heterotypic AZ and homotypic ZZ nucleosomes (referred collectively to as the H2A.Z nucleosomes hereafter) (Luk et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: Forty-four reference regions (called no-Z-zones, covering 152,021 bp and 1,161 nucleosomes) with very low H2A.Z but high H2A occupancy were manually chosen for normalization.
source: Forty-four reference regions (called no-Z-zones, covering 152,021 bp and 1,161 nucleosomes) with very low H2A.Z but high H2A occupancy were manually chosen and were used to normalize the FT fraction data to the input (Figure 1—source data 1 and Figure 1—figure supplement 4A).
evidence: This describes the normalization method used in the qChIP-seq approach.

claim: Under permissive conditions (no RAP), H2A.Z was most prevalent at the +1 nucleosomal positions, less at the -1 positions and progressively less towards the 3' end of genes.
source: Under permissive conditions (no RAP), H2A.Z was most prevalent at the +1 nucleosomal positions (marked by '+'), less at the -1 positions and progressively less towards the 3' end of genes in agreement with published results (Albert et al., 2007) (Figures 1A and B, top, no RAP).
evidence: This is supported by data in Figures 1A and B and citation to previous work.

claim: Rapamycin treatment of TBP-FRB cells for 1 hr resulted in H2A.Z accumulation at the promoter-proximal nucleosomes of most genes, with a corresponding depletion of H2A signal.
source: Rapamycin treatment of TBP-FRB cells for 1 hr resulted in H2A.Z accumulation at the promoter-proximal nucleosomes of most genes, with a corresponding depletion of H2A signal (compare + RAP and no RAP in Figures 1A and C and in Figure 1—figure supplement 5A).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by data in Figures 1A, 1C, and Figure 1—figure supplement 5A.

claim: Rapamycin treatment alone did not cause significant change in histone dynamics as the untagged wild-type cells exhibited similar promoter-specific H2A.Z levels before and after rapamycin treatment.
source: Rapamycin treatment alone did not cause significant change in histone dynamics as the untagged wild-type cells exhibited similar promoter-specific H2A.Z levels before and after rapamycin treatment (Figures 1B and D, Figure 1—figure supplement 5B).
evidence: This is a control experiment shown in Figures 1B, 1D, and Figure 1—figure supplement 5B.

claim: Fifty-six percent of +1 nucleosomes exhibited a significant increase in relative H2A.Z signal upon TBP depletion.
source: Fifty-six percent of +1 nucleosomes exhibited a significant increase in relative H2A.Z signal upon TBP depletion (Figure 1F).
evidence: This is a quantitative result shown in Figure 1F.

claim: Under the permissive condition, the TBP-FRB strain exhibited a higher endogenous H2A.Z occupancy compared to the untagged strain.
source: It is noteworthy that under the permissive condition, the TBP-FRB strain exhibited a higher endogenous H2A.Z occupancy compared to the untagged strain (compare no RAP in Figures 1C and D).
evidence: This observation is noted by comparing data in Figures 1C and 1D.

claim: The difference in endogenous H2A.Z occupancy between TBP-FRB and untagged strains likely reflects a partial defect of the TBP-FRB allele that has predisposed the cells to H2A.Z accumulation.
source: The difference likely reflects a partial defect of the TBP-FRB allele that has predisposed the cells to H2A.Z accumulation.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the observed difference in H2A.Z occupancy.

claim: 72% +1 nucleosomes exhibited an increase in ∆(Z/A) signal upon TBP depletion.
source: As shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 7A, 72% +1 nucleosomes exhibited an increase in ∆(Z/A) signal upon TBP depletion.
evidence: This is a quantitative result shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 7A.

claim: Nuclear depletion of Rpb1-FRB led to strong H2A.Z accumulation and H2A depletion at most promoters.
source: Similar to the results of TBP-FRB removal, nuclear depletion of Rpb1-FRB led to strong H2A.Z accumulation and H2A depletion at most promoters (Figure 1—figure supplement 8 and Figure 1—figure supplement 5C).
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 1—figure supplement 8 and Figure 1—figure supplement 5C.

claim: Sites with strong H2A.Z dynamics are more enriched for endogenous SWR1.
source: Consistent with this idea, sites with strong H2A.Z dynamics are more enriched for endogenous SWR1 (Figure 1—figure supplement 9A).
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 1—figure supplement 9A.

claim: SWR1 dissociated shortly after TBP-FRB depletion as demonstrated by the decrease in Swr1 ChIP signal.
source: Rather than accumulating at the promoters of these two genes, SWR1 dissociated shortly after TBP-FRB depletion as demonstrated by the decrease in Swr1 ChIP signal (Figure 1—figure supplement 9C).
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-qPCR data in Figure 1—figure supplement 9C.

claim: The coincidental accumulation of H2A.Z and depletion of SWR1 suggest that endogenous SWR1 dissociates from promoters after depositing H2A.Z.
source: In addition, the coincidental accumulation of H2A.Z and depletion of SWR1 suggest that endogenous SWR1 dissociates from promoters after depositing H2A.Z.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observed correlation between H2A.Z accumulation and SWR1 depletion.

claim: SWR1 has a lower affinity for the homotypic H2A.Z nucleosome product than the homotypic H2A nucleosome substrate.
source: This is in agreement with the in vitro observation that SWR1 has a lower affinity for the homotypic H2A.Z nucleosome product than the homotypic H2A nucleosome substrate (Ranjan et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: The +1 nucleosomes that exhibited stronger H2A.Z accumulation after TBP depletion are generally more enriched for TFIID.
source: As seen in Figure 2A, the +1 nucleosomes that exhibited stronger H2A.Z accumulation after TBP depletion are generally more enriched for TFIID.
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 2A.

claim: The ribosomal protein (RP) genes are regulated by TFIID and are among the most highly transcribed.
source: The ribosomal protein (RP) genes are regulated by TFIID and are among the most highly transcribed (Rhee and Pugh, 2012; Warner, 1999).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The endogenous +1 nucleosomes of RP genes are generally depleted for H2A.Z but relatively enriched for H2A.
source: Their promoters are unusual in that the endogenous +1 nucleosomes are generally depleted for H2A.Z but relatively enriched for H2A (Figure 2B, n = 128).
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 2B.

claim: Upon depletion of TBP, relative H2A.Z accumulates dramatically at the +1 position of RP genes.
source: Upon depletion of TBP, relative H2A.Z accumulates dramatically at the +1 position (Figure 2B, green).
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 2B.

claim: H2A.Z deposition occurs at the RP gene promoters but H2A.Z nucleosomes are quickly removed by a mechanism that is dependent on TBP, leading to a low steady-state H2A.Z occupancy.
source: The data suggest that H2A.Z deposition occurs at the RP gene promoters but that H2A.Z nucleosomes are quickly removed by a mechanism that is dependent on TBP, leading to a low steady-state H2A.Z occupancy.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data on RP genes.

claim: Rpb1 depletion led to almost no change in H2A.Z occupancy at the +1 nucleosomes of RP genes.
source: Interestingly, Rpb1 depletion led to almost no change in H2A.Z occupancy at the +1 nucleosomes of RP genes (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: H2A.Z removal at the RP genes requires TBP but not Pol II.
source: This suggests that H2A.Z removal at the RP genes requires TBP but not Pol II.
evidence: This is an inference based on the differential effects of TBP and Rpb1 depletion on RP genes.

claim: Before TBP-depletion, the +1 nucleosomes associated with moderately or infrequently transcribing genes exhibited >40% (median) relative H2A.Z occupancy for genes with <16 mRNA/hr.
source: Before TBP-depletion, the +1 nucleosomes associated with moderately or infrequently transcribing genes exhibited >40% (median) relative H2A.Z occupancy for genes with <16 mRNA/hr (n = 3,887) and ~30% (median) for those with 16–50 mRNA/hr (n = 219).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the analysis shown in Figure 2C.

claim: For the top 3% of most highly transcribing genes (>50 mRNA/hr), the steady-state H2A.Z occupancy is ~11% (median) before TBP-depletion.
source: For the top 3% of most highly transcribing genes (>50 mRNA/hr, n = 161) the steady-state H2A.Z occupancy is ~11% (median) before TBP-depletion.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the analysis shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Upon rapamycin treatment, substantial increase of relative H2A.Z occupancy is observed in all transcriptional frequency groups.
source: Upon rapamycin treatment, substantial increase of relative H2A.Z occupancy is observed in all groups (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 2C.

claim: The increase in H2A.Z occupancy upon TBP depletion is more dramatic in the most highly transcribing genes.
source: The increase is more dramatic in the most highly transcribing genes, suggesting that the low steady-state H2A.Z occupancy is due to strong transcriptional activity (Figure 2C, >50 mRNA/hr).
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 2C and represents an interpretation of the data.

claim: H2A.Z accumulated to a smaller extent for the SAGA-enriched genes than for the TFIID-enriched genes among highly transcribing genes.
source: Interestingly, when these highly transcribing genes were sorted based on the enrichment of SAGA or TFIID (Basehoar et al., 2004), H2A.Z accumulated to a smaller extent for the SAGA-enriched genes than for the TFIID-enriched genes (Figure 2C, right).
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 2C.

claim: Low H2A.Z at the strong SAGA-enriched promoters is due to either strong PIC-independent eviction or weak SWR1-mediated H2A.Z deposition or both.
source: Therefore, unlike the strong TFIID-enriched promoters where low steady-state +1 H2A.Z level is due to robust PIC-dependent H2A.Z eviction activity, low H2A.Z at the strong SAGA-enriched promoters is due to either strong PIC-independent eviction or weak SWR1-mediated H2A.Z deposition or both.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the differential behavior of SAGA- and TFIID-enriched promoters.

claim: SWR1 activity of the SWC5-FRB strain was strongly inhibited after 30 min of rapamycin treatment as demonstrated by the robust loss of H2A.Z occupancy.
source: SWR1 activity of the SWC5-FRB strain was strongly inhibited after 30 min of rapamycin treatment as demonstrated by the robust loss of H2A.Z occupancy (Figures 3A–B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A–B).
evidence: This is supported by data in Figures 3A–B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A–B.

claim: When Swc5 was depleted, almost background level of H2A.Z was observed in all transcriptional frequency groups, indicating that robust, constitutive H2A.Z eviction at the +1 position occurs at both active and infrequently transcribed genes.
source: When the relative H2A.Z levels (H2A.Z/input) of the +1 nucleosomes were sorted and grouped by the transcriptional frequency of the downstream genes, almost background level of H2A.Z was observed in all groups, indicating that robust, constitutive H2A.Z eviction at the +1 position occurs at both active and infrequently transcribed genes (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 3C.

claim: At most +1 positions, relative H2A.Z levels dropped below 50% of endogenous levels after 15 min of rapamycin treatment in the SWC5-FRB strain, indicating that the occupancy half-life of H2A.Z is less than 15 min.
source: At most +1 positions, relative H2A.Z levels dropped below 50% of endogenous levels after 15 min of rapamycin treatment, indicating that the occupancy half-life of H2A.Z is less than 15 min.
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: Virtually baseline level of H2A.Z remains after 60 min of rapamycin treatment in the SWC5-FRB strain, suggesting that SWR1 is the sole deposition pathway of H2A.Z at budding yeast promoters.
source: Since virtually baseline level of H2A.Z remains after 60 min of rapamycin treatment (Figure 3—figure supplement 2, red), the data also suggests that SWR1 is the sole deposition pathway of H2A.Z at budding yeast promoters.
evidence: This is an inference based on the complete loss of H2A.Z after prolonged Swc5 depletion.

claim: Depleting both TBP and Swc5 in the double mutant resulted in a less dramatic decrease in relative H2A.Z occupancy at most +1 nucleosomes as compared to the single SWC5-FRB mutant for the same duration (30 min) of rapamycin treatment.
source: Consistent with the idea that the PIC is required for H2A.Z eviction, depleting both TBP and Swc5 in the double mutant resulted in a less dramatic decrease in relative H2A.Z occupancy at most +1 nucleosomes as compared to the single SWC5-FRB mutant for the same duration (i.e. 30 min) of rapamycin treatment (Figures 3D–F and Figure 3—figure supplement 1C–D).
evidence: This is supported by data in Figures 3D–F and Figure 3—figure supplement 1C–D.

claim: TBP depletion did not completely prevent the depletion of H2A.Z caused by Swc5 depletion.
source: It is noteworthy that TBP depletion did not completely prevent the depletion of H2A.Z caused by Swc5 depletion.
evidence: This observation is noted from the double mutant experiment.

claim: One explanation for incomplete prevention of H2A.Z depletion in the double mutant is that the kinetics of TBP depletion by anchor away is slower than that of Swc5.
source: One explanation is that the kinetics of TBP depletion by anchor away is slower than that of Swc5.
evidence: This is a speculative explanation for the observed result.

claim: A PIC-independent H2A.Z eviction pathway might be operating.
source: Alternatively, a PIC-independent H2A.Z eviction pathway might be operating.
evidence: This is a speculative alternative explanation for the observed result.

claim: Cells with INO80-FRB-GFP exhibited slow growth in medium containing both hydroxyurea and rapamycin but not hydroxyurea alone, confirming that INO80 function can be abolished in a rapamycin-dependent manner.
source: Cells with INO80-FRB-GFP (referred to as INO80-FRB hereafter) exhibited slow growth in medium containing both hydroxyurea and rapamycin but not hydroxyurea alone, confirming that INO80 function can be abolished in a rapamycin-dependent manner (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: After 90 min of rapamycin treatment, Ino80 was largely dispersed from the nuclei.
source: After 90 min of rapamycin treatment, Ino80 was largely dispersed from the nuclei (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is supported by microscopy data in Figure 4—figure supplement 1C.

claim: No significant global increase of H2A.Z was observed after Ino80 depletion.
source: No significant global increase of H2A.Z was observed after Ino80 depletion (Figures 4A–C and Figure 4—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by data in Figures 4A–C and Figure 4—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Upon Ino80 depletion, nucleosomal arrays became 'fuzzier' as demonstrated by the general decrease of nucleosomal peak height and the decrease of valley depth at the linker regions.
source: Instead, nucleosomal arrays became 'fuzzier' as demonstrated by the general decrease of nucleosomal peak height and the decrease of valley depth at the linker regions (Figure 4D, top).
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 4D.

claim: In the untagged control (no FRB), the density and positions of the nucleosomal arrays before and after rapamycin treatment were unchanged.
source: By contrast, in the untagged control (no FRB), the density and positions of the nucleosomal arrays before and after rapamycin treatment were unchanged (Figure 4D, middle).
evidence: This is a control result shown in Figure 4D.

claim: 983 genes that require Ino80 for positioning were identified by clustering analysis.
source: Using the difference in nucleosomal density within the linker region between +1 and +2 as a criterion for fuzziness, the chromatin arrays of 983 genes that require Ino80 for positioning were identified by clustering analysis (k = 3).
evidence: This is a result from computational analysis of the data.

claim: Upon Ino80 depletion, the -1 and +1 nucleosomes shifted away from the NDR at genes requiring Ino80 for positioning.
source: The compiled chromatin arrays of these promoters showed, upon Ino80 depletion, the -1 and +1 nucleosomes shifted away from the NDR (Figure 4D, bottom).
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 4D.

claim: The direction of nucleosome shift upon Ino80 depletion is consistent with published results of ino80∆ and is reproducible in both biological replicates.
source: Importantly, the direction of shift at these nucleosomal positions are consistent with the published results of ino80∆ and are reproducible in both biological replicates (Yen et al., 2012) (Figure 4—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 4—figure supplement 1E and citation to previous work.

claim: The data is in agreement with the INO80 remodeler functioning as a histone octamer slider but not an evictor of H2A.Z nucleosomes in vivo.
source: Overall, our data is in agreement with the INO80 remodeler functioning as a histone octamer slider but not an evictor of H2A.Z nucleosomes in vivo (Jeronimo et al., 2015; Shen et al., 2003; Yao et al., 2016; Yen et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data and supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Both TBP and Rpb1 depletion caused histone octamers to reposition away from the NDR.
source: Both TBP and Rpb1 depletion caused histone octamers to reposition away from the NDR (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 5A.

claim: No significant positional shift was observed in the nucleosomal arrays of the control cells upon rapamycin treatment.
source: By contrast, no significant positional shift was observed in the nucleosomal arrays of the control cells (Figure 4D, no FRB).
evidence: This is a control result shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Similar nucleosome repositioning results were previously observed by inactivating the transcription machinery with the rpb1-1 mutant.
source: Similar results were previously observed by inactivating the transcription machinery with the rpb1-1 mutant, which contains a temperature sensitive allele of RPB1 (Weiner et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: The +1 shift upon TBP and Rpb1 depletion was comparatively minor compared to the rpb1-1 data.
source: But unlike the rpb1-1 data, which exhibited strong downstream shift in the +1 nucleosomes under the non-permissive condition, the +1 shift upon TBP and Rpb1 depletion was comparatively minor (Weiner et al., 2010) (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is a comparison with previous work, supported by data in Figure 5A and citation.

claim: The nucleosomal positional shift is progressively more dramatic towards the 3' end of the genes in the TBP and Rpb1 depletion experiments.
source: In fact, the nucleosomal positional shift is progressively more dramatic towards the 3' end of the genes in the TBP and Rpb1 depletion experiments (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 5A.

claim: The positional shift caused by Rpb1 depletion is greater than that caused by TBP depletion.
source: Interestingly, the positional shift caused by Rpb1 depletion is greater than that caused by TBP depletion (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 5A.

claim: One explanation for the difference in positional shift between TBP and Rpb1 depletion is that TBP depletion blocks the Pol II molecules that are initiating but not those that have already engaged in elongation, whereas Rpb1 depletion removes all Pol II from the genome.
source: One explanation for the difference is that TBP depletion blocks the Pol II molecules that are initiating but not those that have already engaged in elongation, whereas Rpb1 depletion removes all Pol II from the genome.
evidence: This is a speculative explanation for the observed difference.

claim: The size of the NDR remains largely unchanged before and after the depletion of TBP or Rpb1 indicating that the formation of the NDR can be established in the absence of the PIC.
source: But in both cases, the size of the NDR remains largely unchanged before and after the depletion of TBP or Rpb1 indicating that the formation of the NDR can be established in the absence of the PIC.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that NDR size is unchanged upon PIC depletion.

claim: The phenomenon of nucleosome downshift in gene body is exaggerated at the RP genes where Pol II-mediated transcriptional activity is very high.
source: The phenomenon of nucleosome downshift in gene body is exaggerated at the RP genes where Pol II-mediated transcriptional activity is very high (Figure 5B) (Warner, 1999).
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 5B and citation to previous work.

claim: The positional shift of the +1 nucleosomes at RP genes is comparatively insignificant upon TBP or Rpb1 depletion.
source: But again, the positional shift of the +1 nucleosomes is comparatively insignificant (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 5B.

claim: A recent study showed repression of the RP genes by heat shock can cause their +1 nucleosomes to shift tens of basepairs in the upstream direction.
source: This observation is important as a recent study showed repression of the RP genes by heat shock can cause their +1 nucleosomes to shift tens of basepairs in the upstream direction, indicating that these +1 nucleosomes are normally pushed downstream when the RP genes are actively transcribed (Reja et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: The data showed that PIC is not responsible for the downstream push of the +1 nucleosomes at RP genes.
source: Our data showed that PIC is not responsible for the downstream push of the +1 nucleosomes and suggests that a chromatin remodeling enzyme(s) might be responsible for setting up the NDR before PIC assembly.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that +1 nucleosomes do not shift significantly upon PIC depletion.

claim: Robust H2A.Z dynamics is generally associated with the +1 nucleosomal position and, to lesser extent, the -1 position.
source: Robust H2A.Z dynamics is generally associated with the +1 nucleosomal position and, to lesser extent, the -1 position [see ∆(Z/A) in Figure 2A, right].
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 2A.

claim: Positive ∆(Z/A) values were more often seen in the upstream region of a promoter with a divergent-oriented gene (Head-Head) than with a tandem-oriented gene (Head-Tail).
source: Indeed, when promoters were sorted based on the orientation of the upstream gene, positive ∆(Z/A) values were more often seen in the upstream region of a promoter with a divergent-oriented gene (Head-Head) than with a tandem-oriented gene (Head-Tail) (Venters and Pugh, 2009) (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 6A.

claim: At divergent promoters separated by a bona fide -1 nucleosome, H2A.Z accumulation was restricted to the +1 positions but not the -1 positions.
source: The difference in H2A.Z dynamics at the +1 and -1 positions is exemplified by 44 divergent promoters that are separated by a bona fide -1 nucleosome (Figure 6—figure supplement 1). At these sites, H2A.Z accumulation was restricted to the +1 positions but not the -1 positions.
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: At the Pol I-dependent RDN37 promoter, depletion of TBP-FRB caused modest H2A.Z depletion and H2A accumulation.
source: Contrastingly, at the Pol I-dependent RDN37 promoter, depletion of TBP-FRB actually caused modest H2A.Z depletion and H2A accumulation (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 6B.

claim: After TBP depletion, the flanking nucleosomes of tRNA genes showed only a subtle increase in H2A.Z.
source: After TBP depletion, the flanking nucleosomes showed only a subtle increase in H2A.Z (Figure 6C).
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 6C.

claim: There is a substantial encroachment of nucleosome density (presumably H2A-containing) within the tRNA gene-associated NDRs upon TBP depletion.
source: However, there is a substantial encroachment of nucleosome density (presumably H2A-containing) within the tRNA gene-associated NDRs (Figures 6C–D).
evidence: This is supported by data in Figures 6C–D.

claim: The assembly or activity of the Pol III transcription machinery is important for creating the NDRs at tRNA genes.
source: These results suggest that the assembly or activity of the Pol III transcription machinery is important for creating the NDRs at these sites.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observed encroachment of nucleosomes into tRNA gene NDRs upon TBP depletion.

claim: Fragile nucleosomes are completely devoid of H2A.Z.
source: Strikingly, fragile nucleosomes are completely devoid of H2A.Z.
evidence: This is supported by data in Figures 6E–F.

claim: When H2A.Z eviction is blocked by TBP depletion, no H2A.Z accumulation was observed at the fragile nucleosome positions.
source: When H2A.Z eviction is blocked by TBP depletion, no H2A.Z accumulation was observed at the fragile nucleosome positions (Figures 6E–F).
evidence: This is supported by data in Figures 6E–F.

claim: H2A.Z deposition does not occur at fragile nucleosome sites.
source: This indicates H2A.Z deposition does not occur at these sites.
evidence: This is an inference based on the lack of H2A.Z at fragile nucleosomes.

claim: H2A.Z deposition and eviction are highly localized at the +1 nucleosomes of Pol II-transcribed genes.
source: Overall, our data suggest that H2A.Z deposition and eviction are highly localized at the +1 nucleosomes of Pol II-transcribed genes.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data on different types of promoters.

claim: The ∆(Z/A) parameter correctly marked the start sites of many previously annotated cryptic unstable transcripts (CUTs) and noncoding RNAs.
source: Indeed, the ∆(Z/A) parameter correctly marked the start sites of many previously annotated cryptic unstable transcripts (CUTs) (Figure 7A, red arrows, CUT531 and CUT445) and noncoding RNAs (Figure 7A, cyan arrows, SUT013 and ICR1) (Bumgarner et al., 2012; Xu et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 7A and citations to previous work.

claim: 4,576 potential +1 nucleosomes were identified by clustering analysis of ∆(Z/A) profiles, of which 3,684 were known +1 nucleosomes.
source: This approach identified 4,576 potential +1 nucleosomes, of which 3,684 were known +1 nucleosomes (n = 6,427) of protein-coding and noncoding genes (Jiang and Pugh, 2009; Kubik et al., 2015; Rhee et al., 2014) (Figure 7—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is a result from computational analysis of the data.

claim: 892 nucleosomes were not previously identified as +1 and could represent novel +1 nucleosomes.
source: The remaining 892 were not previously identified as +1 and therefore could represent novel +1 nucleosomes (Figure 7—figure supplement 1B and Figure 7—source data 1).
evidence: This is a result from computational analysis of the data.

claim: Many of the new +1 nucleosomes are associated with subtle, unannotated CUTs revealed by the rrp6∆ strain.
source: Many of the new +1 nucleosomes are associated with subtle, unannotated CUTs revealed by the rrp6∆ strain (Figure 7B, grey bars).
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 7B.

claim: Global comparison of H2A depletion and H2A.Z accumulation in the absence of the PIC provides a new parameter for transcription start site determination.
source: Therefore global comparison of H2A depletion and H2A.Z accumulation in the absence of the PIC provides a new parameter for transcription start site determination.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the ability of ∆(Z/A) to identify transcription start sites.

claim: The identification of a new +1 nucleosome within the coding region of GDH2 implies that there is a second start site ~1 kb downstream of the first.
source: The identification of a new +1 nucleosome within the coding region of GDH2 implies that there is a second start site ~1 kb downstream of the first (Figure 7C, left, blue arrow).
evidence: This is an inference based on the identification of a new +1 nucleosome, supported by data in Figure 7C.

claim: Microarray mRNA profiling data of wild-type cells showed an elevated mRNA level after the second start site of GDH2 indicating that a population of transcripts was indeed initiated from the internal start site.
source: Concordantly, microarray mRNA profiling data of wild-type cells (Figure 7C, black dots) showed an elevated mRNA level after the second start site indicating that a population of transcripts was indeed initiated from the internal start site (Xu et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 7C and citation to previous work.

claim: In the case of HSE1, the novel start site identified by H2A.Z accumulation is likely the bona fide start site masked by an upstream SUT.
source: In the case of HSE1, the novel start site identified by H2A.Z accumulation is likely the bona fide start site masked by an upstream SUT (Figure 7C, right, blue arrow).
evidence: This is an inference based on the identification of a new +1 nucleosome, supported by data in Figure 7C.

claim: High resolution RNA-seq analysis of nascent Pol II transcripts showed that the originally annotated HSE1 transcribed region consists of two transcripts organized in close tandem.
source: Further high resolution RNA-seq analysis of nascent Pol II transcripts showed that the originally annotated HSE1 transcribed region (Xu et al., 2009) consists of two transcripts organized in close tandem (Figure 7—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 7—figure supplement 1C.

claim: H2A.Z-enriched nucleosomes that flank an NDR within the Ty3 retrotransposon accumulated H2A.Z after TBP-FRB depletion, implying the presence of a pair of divergent promoters.
source: In another example, H2A.Z-enriched nucleosomes that flank an NDR within the Ty3 retrotransposon accumulated H2A.Z (and lost H2A) after TBP-FRB depletion, implying the presence of a pair of divergent promoters (Figure 7D).
evidence: This is an inference based on the pattern of H2A.Z accumulation, supported by data in Figure 7D.

claim: Nascent Pol II RNA data and standard RNA-seq analysis of mRNA confirmed the presence of transcripts initiated from sites within the Ty3 retrotransposon.
source: Indeed, our nascent Pol II RNA data, as well as standard RNA-seq analysis of mRNA, confirmed the presence of transcripts initiated from these sites (Figure 7D and Figure 7—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 7D and Figure 7—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Cryptic antisense transcription has been reported for the Ty1 retrotransposon and the antisense Ty1 CUT is important for gene silencing and suppression of Ty1 mobility.
source: Cryptic antisense transcription has been reported for the Ty1 retrotransposon and the antisense Ty1 CUT is important for gene silencing and suppression of Ty1 mobility (Berretta et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: The antisense Ty3 CUT identified may play a similar role to the antisense Ty1 CUT.
source: Therefore, the antisense Ty3 CUT identified here may play a similar role (Figure 7D, gray bar).
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on the similarity to Ty1.

claim: Rapid, constitutive turnover of H2A.Z occurs genome-wide, even at infrequently transcribing genes.
source: This work demonstrates that rapid, constitutive turnover of H2A.Z occurs genome-wide, even at infrequently transcribing genes.
evidence: This is a primary conclusion of the study.

claim: At the nucleosomes covering or immediately downstream of the start sites of Pol II transcripts, the relative enrichment of H2A.Z is a steady state maintained by two major opposing forces imposed by the SWR1 complex and the transcription machinery.
source: At the nucleosomes covering or immediately downstream of the start sites of Pol II transcripts, the relative enrichment of H2A.Z is a steady state maintained by two major opposing forces imposed by the SWR1 complex and the transcription machinery.
evidence: This is a primary conclusion of the study.

claim: SWR1 converts H2A nucleosomes to the H2A.Z-containing forms and the transcription machinery then actively disassembles them.
source: SWR1 converts H2A nucleosomes to the H2A.Z-containing forms (Figure 8, step I) and the transcription machinery then actively disassembles them.
evidence: This is a primary conclusion of the study, illustrated in Figure 8.

claim: Preventing PIC assembly by TBP or Pol II removal could allow more SWR1 to bind the NDR leading to H2A.Z accumulation.
source: One explanation for the increase in H2A.Z levels at the +1 promoter upon TBP depletion is that the balance between H2A.Z eviction and deposition of H2A.Z nucleosomes by SWR1 has been disrupted. SWR1 continues to convert H2A nucleosomes to the H2A.Z containing forms but with no eviction to restore these nucleosomes back to the AA state in the absence of the PIC.
evidence: This is a speculative explanation for the observed H2A.Z accumulation.

claim: The data argue against the hypothesis that TBP depletion leads to aberrant SWR1 recruitment.
source: Our data argue against this hypothesis in that Swr1 occupancy decreased, rather than increased, in response to TBP depletion.
evidence: This is based on the ChIP-qPCR data showing decreased Swr1 occupancy.

claim: It is the SWR1 complex already residing at the NDR before TBP depletion that is responsible for the increased H2A.Z deposition.
source: Therefore, it is the SWR1 complex already residing at the NDR before TBP depletion that is responsible for the increased H2A.Z deposition.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that Swr1 occupancy decreases upon TBP depletion.

claim: The observation that Swr1 occupancy decreased upon TBP depletion most likely reflects the lower affinity of SWR1 for the H2A.Z nucleosome relative to the H2A nucleosome.
source: The observation that Swr1 occupancy decreased upon TBP depletion is interesting as it most likely reflects the lower affinity of SWR1 for the H2A.Z nucleosome relative to the H2A nucleosome (Ranjan et al., 2015).
evidence: This is an interpretation based on previous in vitro findings, supported by citation.

claim: After SWR1 has generated the H2A.Z nucleosome product, the enzyme dissociates from the NDR.
source: As such, after SWR1 has generated the H2A.Z nucleosome product, the enzyme dissociates from the NDR.
evidence: This is an inference based on the lower affinity of SWR1 for H2A.Z nucleosomes.

claim: Inhibition of transcription could decrease histone acetylation, and thus indirectly impair SWR1 recruitment.
source: Alternatively but not exclusively, since optimal SWR1 recruitment requires H3 and H4 tail acetylation, inhibition of transcription could decrease histone acetylation, and thus indirectly impair SWR1 recruitment (Liu et al., 2005; Raisner et al., 2005; Ranjan et al., 2013).
evidence: This is a speculative alternative explanation, supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Perturbation of PIC assembly causes promoter-specific H2A.Z, but not H2A, to accumulate, suggesting that the constitutive disassembly occurs preferentially with H2A.Z-containing nucleosomes.
source: Perturbation of PIC assembly causes promoter-specific H2A.Z, but not H2A, to accumulate, suggesting that the constitutive disassembly occurs preferentially with H2A.Z-containing nucleosomes (Figure 8, steps II-a and II-b).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental findings.

claim: It is not known whether the heterotypic AZ or the homotypic ZZ form is the preferred nucleosomal state for disassembly.
source: Currently, it is not known whether the heterotypic AZ or the homotypic ZZ form is the preferred nucleosomal state for disassembly as our experiments did not distinguish between these forms.
evidence: This acknowledges a limitation of the current study.

claim: One explanation for the preference of H2A.Z eviction is that the PIC preferentially assembles on promoters that have a +1 H2A.Z nucleosome.
source: One explanation for the preference of H2A.Z eviction is that the PIC preferentially assembles on promoters that have a +1 H2A.Z nucleosome.
evidence: This is a speculative explanation for the observed preference.

claim: Optimal TBP recruitment during oleate induction requires H2A.Z.
source: Consistent with this idea, optimal TBP recruitment during oleate induction requires H2A.Z and the C-terminal domain of H2A.Z has been reported to bind RNA Pol II (Adam et al., 2001; Wan et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: H2A.Z-containing nucleosomes may be preferentially recognized by the PIC for disassembly.
source: Another nonexclusive possibility is that H2A.Z-containing nucleosomes are preferentially recognized by the PIC for disassembly.
evidence: This is a speculative alternative explanation.

claim: Rapid induction of GAL1-10, PHO5 and the heat-responsive genes requires H2A.Z and is accompanied by preferential eviction of H2A.Z over H2A.
source: In support of this idea, rapid induction of GAL1-10, PHO5 and the heat-responsive genes requires H2A.Z and is accompanied by preferential eviction of H2A.Z over H2A (Santisteban et al., 2000; Venters et al., 2011; Zhang et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The eviction of H2A.Z is, at least in part, coupled to some steps during transcription, rather than an independent process upstream of PIC assembly.
source: But regardless of the basis of how the preference for H2A.Z removal is achieved, our data suggest that the eviction of H2A.Z is, at least in part, coupled to some steps during transcription, rather than an independent process upstream of PIC assembly (Figure 8, step II-b).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental findings.

claim: A recent report showed that inactivation of transcription by temperature sensitive alleles rpb1-1 and tbp ts-1 led to promoter-proximal H3 accumulation.
source: A recent report that utilized ChIP and qPCR to monitor histone H3 occupancy showed that inactivation of transcription by the temperature sensitive alleles rpb1-1 and tbp ts-1, led to promoter-proximal H3 accumulation, suggesting that the PIC is required to maintain an open chromatin state at the +1 position that is depleted of all histones (Ansari et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: In the current study, the input nucleosomal levels at the +1 positions were largely unchanged for most genes upon TBP (or Rpb1) depletion.
source: In the current study, the input nucleosomal levels at the +1 positions were largely unchanged for most genes upon TBP (or Rpb1) depletion.
evidence: This is a result from the current study.

claim: The discrepancy between the current study and previous work may be an artifact caused by a normalization step that equalizes the input tag counts of all samples.
source: This discrepancy may be an artifact caused by a normalization step in our study that equalizes the input tag counts of all samples.
evidence: This is a speculative explanation for the discrepancy.

claim: The qChIP-seq approach reports H2A.Z IP efficiency, so even if the input nucleosome occupancy were higher in the TBP depleted sample, the absolute increase of H2A.Z would be greater, further supporting the conclusion.
source: But because the qChIP-seq approach reports H2A.Z IP efficiency, even if the input nucleosome occupancy were indeed higher in the TBP depleted sample, the absolute increase of H2A.Z would in fact be greater in response to TBP depletion, further supporting our conclusion.
evidence: This is a logical argument about the interpretation of the data.

claim: The TBP depleted sample does not appear to be severely undercounted, as the least transcribed genes exhibited similar input nucleosome densities after normalization.
source: Furthermore, the TBP depleted sample does not appear to be severely undercounted, as the least transcribed genes (bottom 3%) exhibited similar input nucleosome densities after normalization (Figure 1—figure supplement 10).
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 1—figure supplement 10.

claim: Another group previously used MNase-seq to probe the change of chromatin organization in the rpb1-1 mutant and showed that the +1 nucleosomes also did not accumulate when transcription was blocked.
source: Interestingly, another group has previously used MNase-seq to probe the change of chromatin organization in the rpb1-1 mutant and showed that the +1 nucleosomes also did not accumulate when transcription was blocked (Weiner et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: PIC-dependent disassembly of the +1 H2A.Z nucleosomes involves some metastable sub-nucleosomal intermediates.
source: We speculate that PIC-dependent disassembly of the +1 H2A.Z nucleosomes involves some metastable sub-nucleosomal intermediates (Ramachandran et al., 2015; Rhee et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation, supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The DNA associated with sub-nucleosomal species is likely hypersensitive to MNase digestion and would be underrepresented in the input fraction.
source: Since the DNA associated with the sub-nucleosomal species is likely hypersensitive to MNase digestion, it would be underrepresented in our input fraction.
evidence: This is a speculative explanation for the observed results.

claim: Standard H3 ChIP is likely less biased against the sub-nucleosomal species and therefore revealed H3 accumulation when transcription was blocked.
source: By contrast, standard H3 ChIP is likely less biased against the sub-nucleosomal species and therefore revealed H3 accumulation when transcription was blocked (Ansari et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a speculative explanation for the discrepancy with previous work, supported by citation.

claim: Earlier electron microscopy and genome-wide mapping studies place the PIC immediately upstream of the TSS on the DNA.
source: Earlier electron microscopy and genome-wide mapping studies place the PIC immediately upstream of the TSS on the DNA, suggesting that the +1 H2A.Z nucleosome and the PIC (in the closed conformation) can coexist in many promoters (Murakami et al., 2013; Rhee and Pugh, 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Promoter scanning mediated by TFIIH is speculated to be the driving force for H2A.Z eviction.
source: However, we speculate that promoter scanning mediated by TFIIH is the driving force (Figure 8, step II-b).
evidence: This is a speculative hypothesis.

claim: A single-molecule study showed that yeast PIC repeatedly scans the promoter over an extended region (85 base pairs on average), leading to cycles of transcription bubble formation and collapse before committing to promoter escape.
source: A recent single-molecule study showed that yeast PIC repeatedly scans the promoter over an extended region (85 base pairs on average), leading to cycles of transcription bubble formation and collapse before committing to promoter escape (Fazal et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Formation of extended transcription bubbles in the NDR will overwind the DNA downstream, leading to a propensity to form positive supercoils in the +1 nucleosomal region.
source: Formation of such extended transcription bubbles in the NDR will overwind the DNA downstream, leading to a propensity to form positive supercoils in the +1 nucleosomal region.
evidence: This is a speculative mechanistic explanation.

claim: Positive supercoiling will likely destabilize the +1 nucleosome.
source: Given that DNA wraps the histone octamer in a left-handed turn (i.e. negative writhe) and that the promoter-distal end of the nucleosome is restricted to rotate freely, positive supercoiling will likely destabilize the +1 nucleosome.
evidence: This is a speculative mechanistic explanation based on nucleosome structure.

claim: Repeated cycles of futile scanning without promoter escape may also occur at infrequently transcribing genes explaining the constitutive H2A.Z dynamics at those promoters.
source: Repeated cycles of futile scanning without promoter escape may also occur at infrequently transcribing genes explaining the constitutive H2A.Z dynamics at those promoters.
evidence: This is a speculative explanation for the observed H2A.Z dynamics at infrequently transcribed genes.

claim: A subsequent step of transcription, such as promoter escape or elongation, may be the driving force for H2A.Z eviction.
source: Although we favor a model in which H2A.Z eviction is a direct consequence of the initiation process, we cannot exclude the possibility that a subsequent step of transcription, such as promoter escape or elongation, is the driving force as TBP depletion blocks all steps of transcription.
evidence: This acknowledges an alternative possibility.

claim: TBP or the integrity of the PIC may be required to recruit another factor that functions to disassemble H2A.Z nucleosomes.
source: We also cannot exclude TBP or the integrity of the PIC may be required to recruit another factor that functions to disassemble H2A.Z nucleosomes.
evidence: This acknowledges another alternative possibility.

claim: Robust PIC-dependent H2A.Z eviction occurs even at promoters that infrequently fire, providing an opportunity to use H2A.Z dynamics as a parameter to locate initiation sites.
source: Since robust PIC-dependent H2A.Z eviction occurs even at promoters that infrequently fire, this provides an opportunity to use H2A.Z dynamics as a parameter to locate initiation sites that were previously missed by the conventional transcript mapping approach (Xu et al., 2009).
evidence: This is a conclusion about the utility of the H2A.Z dynamics parameter.

claim: Sites with strong H2A.Z dynamics were able to identify initiation sites of protein coding genes, SUTs and CUTs, as well as sites masked by upstream transcripts.
source: Sites with strong H2A.Z dynamics were able to identify not only initiation sites of protein coding genes, SUTs and CUTs, but also sites that are masked by upstream transcripts.
evidence: This is a conclusion about the utility of the H2A.Z dynamics parameter, supported by data in Figure 7.

claim: The H2A.Z dynamics approach cannot pinpoint the location of a TSS at base pair resolution, but sites are generally restricted within the identified +1 nucleosome near the edge adjacent to the NDR.
source: Although this approach cannot pinpoint the location of a TSS at base pair resolution, the sites are generally restricted within the identified +1 nucleosome near the edge adjacent to the NDR.
evidence: This acknowledges a limitation of the approach.

claim: The direction of the predicted transcripts can be inferred based on the location of the NDR and is almost always pointing away from the NDR.
source: Importantly, since PIC-dependent H2A.Z eviction is linked to an NDR, the direction of the predicted transcripts can be inferred based on the location of the NDR and is almost always pointing away from the NDR.
evidence: This is a conclusion about the utility of the H2A.Z dynamics parameter.

claim: The H2A.Z dynamics approach may not identify the TSSs of promoters that are associated with low endogenous H2A.Z deposition activity and/or have low PIC-dependent H2A.Z eviction activity as in the case of the SAGA-dominating promoters.
source: Another limitation of this approach is that it may not identify the TSSs of promoters that are associated with low endogenous H2A.Z deposition activity and/or have low PIC-dependent H2A.Z eviction activity as in the case of the SAGA-dominating promoters.
evidence: This acknowledges another limitation of the approach.

claim: Evidence supporting INO80's role in evicting H2A.Z comes from in vitro experiments and in vivo experiments showing global increase of H2A.Z occupancy in ino80∆ or arp5∆ strains.
source: Evidence supporting this idea comes from in vitro experiments showing that the INO80 complex can mediate a reaction that replaces the nucleosomal H2A.Z-H2B dimer with H2A-H2B, which supposedly opposes the reaction catalyzed by SWR1 (Papamichos-Chronakis et al., 2011), as well as in vivo experiments showing a global increase of H2A.Z occupancy in ino80∆ or arp5∆ (both components of the INO80 complex) strains (Papamichos-Chronakis et al., 2006; Yen et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The current experiments agree with the study showing ino80∆ mutants exhibited normal H2A.Z occupancy at promoters, arguing that INO80 does not contribute to global eviction of H2A.Z.
source: Our experiments agree with the latter study arguing that INO80 does not contribute to global eviction of H2A.Z, as no accumulation of H2A.Z was observed when Ino80 was depleted.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental findings.

claim: One explanation for the discrepancy between studies on INO80's role is that ino80∆ and arp5∆ are both associated with genome instability, resulting in aneuploidy that complicates the interpretation of genomic data.
source: One explanation for the discrepancy between these various experiments is that ino80∆ and arp5∆ are both associated with genome instability, resulting in aneuploidy that complicates the interpretation of genomic data (Chambers et al., 2012 and Ashby Morrison personal communication).
evidence: This is a speculative explanation for the discrepancy, supported by citation and personal communication.

claim: H2A.Z occupancy was assayed within two hours of conditionally depleting Ino80 from the nucleus to minimize aneuploidy.
source: To circumvent this problem, we assayed H2A.Z occupancy within two hours of conditionally depleting Ino80 from the nucleus, thereby minimizing aneuploidy.
evidence: This describes a methodological approach to address a potential confound.

claim: Standard microarray normalization and ChIP-exo may not be ideal for comparing H2A.Z occupancy in different strains.
source: Furthermore, the previous studies used ChIP-chip and ChIP-exo to measure H2A.Z occupancy (Jeronimo et al., 2015; Papamichos-Chronakis et al., 2011; Yen et al., 2013). However, these approaches may not be ideal for comparing H2A.Z occupancy in different strains.
evidence: This is a critique of previous methodologies.

claim: Standard microarray normalization involves scaling with data averages that could mask any global occupancy change.
source: Standard microarray normalization involves scaling with data averages that could mask any global occupancy change (Quackenbush, 2002).
evidence: This is a critique of previous methodologies, supported by citation.

claim: ChIP-exo measures the distribution of crosslinking points between the immunoprecipitated protein and DNA that could be influenced by variation of crosslinking efficiency in mutants with chromatin dynamics defects.
source: ChIP-exo measures the distribution of crosslinking points between the immunoprecipitated protein and DNA that could be influenced by variation of crosslinking efficiency in mutants with chromatin dynamics defects (Yen et al., 2013).
evidence: This is a critique of previous methodologies.

claim: The qChIP-seq approach takes into account the input, flow-through, and IP fractions of each IP reaction and uses the immuno-depleted signal in the flow-through to scale the IP signal.
source: The qChIP-seq approach conducted here takes into account the input, flow-through, and IP fractions of each IP reaction and uses the immuno-depleted signal in the flow-through to scale the IP signal.
evidence: This describes the methodological approach used in the current study.

claim: The qChIP-seq occupancy data reflects IP efficiency relative to input at individual nucleosomal sites and is not influenced by global occupancy change.
source: Therefore, occupancy data reflects IP efficiency relative to input at individual nucleosomal sites and is not influenced by global occupancy change.
evidence: This describes an advantage of the qChIP-seq approach.

claim: The qChIP-seq approach is less sensitive to variation in crosslinking efficiency as formaldehyde crosslinking serves only to preserve the histone-DNA interaction during the pull down.
source: It is also less sensitive to variation in crosslinking efficiency as formaldehyde crosslinking serves only to preserve the histone-DNA interaction during the pull down.
evidence: This describes an advantage of the qChIP-seq approach.

claim: Ino80 depletion did not cause H2A.Z accumulation, arguing against the INO80 remodeler being the main evictor of H2A.Z in the constitutive turnover process.
source: Our data showed that Ino80 depletion did not cause H2A.Z accumulation, arguing against the INO80 remodeler being the main evictor of H2A.Z in the constitutive turnover process.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental findings.

claim: The observation that INO80 is not involved in constitutive H2A.Z eviction is not inconsistent with INO80 being recruited to remodel specific promoters in response to induction as seen in the PHO5 and GAL genes.
source: This observation however is not inconsistent with INO80 being recruited to remodel specific promoters in response to induction as seen in the PHO5 and GAL genes (Barbaric et al., 2007; Rosonina et al., 2014).
evidence: This reconciles the current findings with previous work, supported by citations.

claim: INO80 contributes to the positioning of nucleosomes near the promoters.
source: Although INO80 is not involved in the constitutive eviction of H2A.Z at the +1 positions, our data suggest that INO80 does contribute to the positioning of nucleosomes near the promoters.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental findings.

claim: The sliding defect associated with Ino80 depletion is reproducible and consistent with previous studies.
source: While the sliding defect associated with Ino80 depletion is reproducible and consistent with previous studies (Yao et al., 2016; Yen et al., 2012), the defect is small compared to that associated with mutants in genes encoding other chromatin remodelers, such as RSC, CHD1, ISW1, and ISW2 (Gkikopoulos et al., 2011; Hartley and Madhani, 2009; Ocampo et al., 2016; Whitehouse et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by data and citations to previous work.

claim: The role of INO80 in nucleosome positioning could be indirect or redundant with another remodeling factor.
source: Therefore, the role of INO80 in nucleosome positioning could be indirect or redundant with another remodeling factor.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the relatively small effect of INO80 depletion.

claim: ATP-dependent remodelers, such as RSC, are recruited to the promoter region by sequence specific DNA-binding factors to establish the NDR.
